reason: The cited evidence (E1) only supports the premise that MoS₂ is a good solid lubricant below 400 °C and that it can be incorporated into HEAs via powder metallurgy. It provides no evidence for dopant stabilization of MoS₂, laser cladding as a processing route, or the claimed high-temperature performance up to 800 °C. The key premises regarding high-temperature stability and the specific intervention are unsupported.
premises: MoS₂ provides good lubricating performance below 400 °C
MoS₂ can be incorporated into HEAs via powder metallurgy
Dopants can stabilize MoS₂ against oxidation above 450–500 °C
Laser cladding can produce a well-dispersed, metallurgically bonded composite layer
Stabilized MoS₂ will regulate oxide formation and maintain lubrication up to 800 °C
